content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I’m trying to find out if it’s possible to view the [product_name] webserver on an HMI KTP700 panel.

I don’t think that’s possible. Typically, you need a browser like Internet Explorer on a PC to access the webserver. The panel display usually doesn’t have a suitable browser, but you could design your own pages using [product_name] software.

You could attempt the following: Within the controls, there’s an 'HTML browser' control. In the properties (URL), input the IP address of the [product_name], for example: 'http://192.168.178.32/logo_login.shtm?!App-Language=1'.

If your KTP panel does have a browser built in, I may need to revise my previous statement. In this scenario, I believe the internal webserver would be utilized. However, the extended webserver isn’t particularly beneficial on these panels since their programming capabilities surpass those offered by the [product_name] web editor.

Hi, I tried using the HTML browser control but couldn’t configure it correctly. After inserting the URL, I received error code 99, which you can see in the attached image. I also followed another guide from [url], but that didn’t work either; I got error code 3. Upon further research, it appears that my KTP700 Basic doesn't support the HTML browser. Is there something I’m overlooking, or is it simply not possible?

The linked page indicates that the HTML browser feature is only available on Comfort Panels. If you have a Basic Panel, that might be the issue. There’s also a note stating that only simple HTML can be used—so it appears the browser feature isn’t available for your device.

I started over and managed to reach the [product_name] webserver login screen. I’ve attached a video showing that whenever I try to log in, the page just refreshes without granting access. Any tips? It seems that Basic Panels don’t allow internet access, though you can reach local devices.

In your video, you show that the customized webserver option is selected. Have you created a website using [product_name] Web Editor and saved it to an SD card inserted in the [product_name]? If not, try disabling that option. If you have, is the website accessible from a PC? I’m not certain what 'simple HTML' entails, but the [product_name] websites also require JavaScript.

Yes, I have used the [product_name] Web Editor, placed the SD card in the [product_name], and can access it from both PC and VPN without issues. Still, if I am able to reach the login site, I don’t understand why I’m unable to proceed.

For the login page, 'simple HTML' is used, but you need JavaScript for full functionality. Did you read the entire post or just the beginning? Try exploring more parts yourself, but I doubt it will work. As mentioned before, using a customized website doesn’t make much sense since the KTP HMI panels support more features than the web editor.
Hello, were you able to successfully open the [product_name] webserver on the KTP700 Basic panel?

analysis.insight_summary: The main user challenge involves trying to operate the [product_name] webserver from a KTP700 Basic HMI panel. The user reaches the login screen but cannot log in, likely due to the panel’s limited browser capabilities and lack of JavaScript support. The discussion reveals incomplete documentation about HTML browser controls and compatibility on Basic Panels, resulting in user confusion and interrupted workflows.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to fully access, view, and interact with the [product_name] webserver interface on the KTP700 Basic HMI panel, with functions available similar to PC access.
